messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: plots unaffected by alpha (mac)
parts:
Hi all,

I'm new to the package, and just spent some time tonight starting the
book that was put online (thanks for that). Things were going fine
until I hit the scatterplot example which used transparency to deal
with over-plotting. The alpha argument doesn't seem to have any effect
on my system.

qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds, alpha = I(1/10000))

and

qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds)

produce exactly the same plots (no transparency in either). I tried
using Quartz, Xterm, and Java (via JGR) with similar results.

Thoughts? Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Sincerely,
Ian
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> p<-qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds, alpha = I(1/1000))
> summary(p)
data: carat, cut, color, clarity, depth, table, price, x, y, z
[53940x10]
mapping: x = carat, y = price
scales: x, y
faceting: facet_grid(. ~ ., FALSE)
-----------------------------------
geom_point: alpha = 0.001
stat_identity: alpha = 0.001
position_identity: (width = NULL, height = NULL)

> sessionInfo()

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: plots unaffected by alpha (mac)
parts:
Hi Ian -

On my mac the first command you provide plots (seemingly) nothing, and
the second plots the points fine. The reason the first does not is
that the alpha level is too low, so if you enter

qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds, alpha = 1/50)

you should see the transparency. I think Hadley told me that the
limit is 1/256, so that you have to stack 256 points on top of each
other to get the opaque color. Now, in the new version (0.8.3) alpha
was added as an aesthetic as well, so if you want it can vary with the
data just as something like a size can (i.e., it doesn't have to be
fixed for every point like 1/256).

Make sure that you have the new version installed.
( install.packages('ggplot2') )

In any case, something like this should run without any problems -

ggplot(aes(x = carat, y = price), data = diamonds) +
geom_point(colour = alpha('black', 1/50))

Does that help?

david.

PS - if you installed the new version of ggplot2 more than a few days
ago, reinstall it; there were problems uploading versions to the CRAN
which were recently fixed.

parts:
Hum... on my PC everything works fine, but on my mac both of the
following produce identical (non-transparent) results:

> qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds, alpha = I(1/50))

Your explicitly layered call does produce the correct result though:

> ggplot(aes(x = carat, y = price), data = diamonds) +
+ geom_point(colour = alpha('black', 1/50))

so does

qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds, colour = I(alpha("black",1/50)))

I just installed the package last night, so it should be the latest
version. I'll see if upgrading to 2.9.0 helps, but looking at the
documentation, I don't see why 'alpha=I(1/50)' should even work. The
docs imply that it should be going into the ... argument, which is
then passed to geom_point. geom_point doesn't have an alpha argument,
so again it goes into the ... but this is "unused" according to it's
documentation, so how is my system's behavior not expected?
